feedback_text: Patient admitted for management of cardiovascular complications. During discharge education, patient expressed significant difficulty understanding new multi-drug cardiac medication schedule. Previous chart history confirms non-compliant behavior with diuretic therapy. Patient reported confusion regarding fluid restriction targets. Urgent outpatient follow-up recommended within 7 days.

Patient presented via emergency department with acute symptoms. Discharge counseling was expedited due to high departmental census. Patient appeared confused about follow-up steps and outpatient clinic referral location. Records indicate patient previously missed scheduled follow-up visits. High risk of post-discharge readmission noted.

Routine discharge protocol completed with family physician and primary caregiver present. Caregiver actively engaged and confirmed medication list. Patient reported no difficulty with daily activities or understanding instructions. Follow-up appointment scheduled at community health center in 14 days.

Comprehensive internal medicine review completed prior to discharge. Patient demonstrated clear comprehension of oral hypoglycemic medications and insulin self-administration. Patient asked relevant questions and affirmed confidence in following post-discharge regimen without confusion. No acute barriers to follow-up noted.

Evaluation of renal function parameters stable for discharge. However, patient expressed feeling confused about stringent dietary potassium and fluid restrictions. Patient acknowledged difficulty balancing dietary limitations with diabetes meal planning. Outpatient renal dietary counseling referral initiated.
Inpatient stay concluded with stable vital signs. Postpartum and postoperative care reviewed in detail with patient and partner. No concerns or questions voiced; follow-up visit arranged.

Discharge instructions given to patient. Note indicates patient previously missed a follow-up physical therapy rehabilitation session. Patient reported some confusion regarding weight-bearing restrictions. Emphasized necessity of strict adherence to rehabilitation protocol.

Mobility assessment demonstrated safe transfer and ambulation with assistive device. Physical therapy home exercises reviewed with patient and spouse. No cognitive impairment or instructions confusion observed. Home health therapy scheduled.

Multidisciplinary psychiatric evaluation completed. Patient demonstrated clear understanding of safety crisis plan and outpatient psychotropic medication management. Family member confirmed supervision. No confusion noted regarding emergency contact resources.

Patient treated for respiratory compromise. During discharge teach-back, patient experienced persistent difficulty demonstrating proper inhaler and spacer technique despite repeated nursing instruction. Follow-up respiratory therapy visit strongly advised within 5 days.
Procedure completed without immediate complication. Note: No direct discharge counseling or patient education documented for this department as service was limited to procedural imaging consult.

Cardiothoracic surgical recovery progress reviewed. Patient reported considerable confusion regarding sternal precautions and post-discharge physical activity restrictions. Nurse navigator scheduled outreach call to address patient difficulty with daily self-monitoring.

Post-operative course was uneventful. Incision clean, dry, and intact. Detailed wound care instructions provided verbally and in printed format. Patient confirmed understanding of infection signs and pain medication tapering. Follow-up surgical clinic visit booked.
Post-procedure catheter care and hydration guidelines thoroughly reviewed. Patient verbalized complete understanding and reported no confusion or discomfort. Routine outpatient follow-up scheduled.
